concept.technique_name: clue-word and pivot analysis for multi-blank text completion

examples.problem_statement: The more deeply one delves into the relevant literature, the more apparent it becomes that psychoanalysis is a practice (i) ___________. Even tenets that some might deem (ii) __________ to the general philosophy, such as the notion that the human psyche is primarily governed by conflicting desires and is formed in large part by early childhood experiences, are by no means accepted as gospel, even by some of its most (iii) ___________. Blank (i): teeming with ridicule / devoid of substance / rife with contention. Blank (ii): critical / immaterial / anathema. Blank (iii): esteemed beneficiaries / quarrelsome factions / seasoned practitioners.

solution.operation: Extract the revealing clue words: gospel, tenet, even
solution.result: gospel = "accepted fact" or "agreed-upon truth"; tenet = "accepted principle"; even = a pivot signalling contrast
solution.description: Before touching any blank, pin down the words that carry the sentence's logic. Note that gospel here takes its secondary sense of agreed-upon truth rather than its religious sense, that tenet also means an accepted principle, and that even flags a relationship of surprise.

solution.operation: Apply the pivot even to blank (ii): the tenets deemed ___ are by no means accepted as gospel, and that should be surprising
solution.description: Start with the second blank because even tells you to be surprised that these tenets are not accepted truth. Surprise only arises if the tenets are crucial to the general philosophy, so the blank must mean central or critical.

solution.operation: Apply the second even to blank (iii): even the most ___ do not accept the central tenets
solution.description: Again the even marks something contrary to expectation, so fill the blank with the group you would most expect to subscribe to the field's central tenets: the people most experienced in it, the seasoned practitioners.

solution.operation: Carry the second sentence's disagreement back into blank (i): psychoanalysis is a practice ___
solution.description: With blanks (ii) and (iii) settled, the second sentence establishes that even the most experienced practitioners disagree about the fundamental tenets. Describe the field accordingly as subject to great debate.

examples.answer: Rife with contention, critical, seasoned practitioners

key_reminders: In this context gospel means accepted fact or agreed-upon truth, not the religious sense.
A tenet is an accepted principle of a field.
The word even is a pivot signalling a relationship contrary to expectation; use it to set the direction of the blank.
common_mistakes: Filling blank (i) first, when the even pivot makes blank (ii) the only blank with a determinate clue.
Reading gospel in its religious sense and losing the accepted-truth logic that drives blank (ii).
Choosing quarrelsome factions for blank (iii): the sentence needs the group you would expect to agree, not one already defined by disagreement.

concept.technique_name: factoring out a common power, then prime factorization

examples.problem_statement: If x = 4^{20} + 4^{21} + 4^{22}, what is the greatest prime factor of x?

solution.description: All three terms contain 4^{20}, so pull that common power out of the sum, leaving each term divided by 4^{20} inside the parentheses.
Evaluate the small powers inside the parentheses and add them, which collapses the bracket to the single number 21.

solution.operation: Take the prime factors of each part of 4^{20}(21)
solution.result: prime factors are 2 from 4^{20}, and 3 and 7 from 21
solution.description: Read off the primes of the factored form: the 4^{20} term contributes only 2, and the 21 term contributes 3 and 7.
Pick the largest of the three prime factors found.

key_reminders: A sum of powers with the same base can be factored by pulling out the lowest power.
The prime factors of a product are the union of the prime factors of its factors.
common_mistakes: Trying to evaluate 4^{20} + 4^{21} + 4^{22} numerically instead of factoring out the common power.
Stopping at 21 and reporting 21 as the answer without splitting it into 3 and 7.

examples.problem_statement: Select the two answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning. Some scientists argue that carbon compounds play such a central role in life on Earth because of the possibility of ______ resulting from the carbon atom's ability to form an unending series of different molecules. Choices: A diversity, B deviation, C variety, D reproduction, E stability, F invigoration.

solution.operation: Locate the phrase that governs the blank: "the ability to form an unending series of different molecules"
solution.result: the blank must name what an unending series of different molecules makes possible
solution.description: Find the part of the sentence that tells you how to fill the blank; here the trailing phrase about unending and different molecules is the key indicator.

solution.result: diversity and variety both fit logically
solution.description: Check which words follow from many different molecules. Diversity and variety clearly do, and each produces a sentence that means the same as the other.

solution.operation: Check whether any other pairing of the six choices yields two sentences alike in meaning
solution.result: no other pair produces sentences as similar in meaning
solution.description: Sentence equivalence requires a matched pair, so confirm that the remaining choices cannot be paired into two equivalent sentences before committing.

examples.answer: Choice A: diversity AND Choice C: variety

key_reminders: The correct pair must both fit the sentence and produce two sentences alike in meaning.
Fill the blank from the sentence's own key phrase rather than from general plausibility.
common_mistakes: Selecting a single word that fits well without checking that a second choice makes a sentence alike in meaning.
Picking deviation on the strength of "different" alone, which does not match the sense of an unending series of molecules.
